questions.q: The larger of two angles made with the& $X$-axis of a straight line drawn through $( 1, 2 )$ so that it intersects the line $x + y = 4$ at a point distant $\sqrt{6} / 3$ from the point $( 1, 2 )$ is
questions.solution:
Let $A = ( 1, 2 )$ equation of line is

$\dfrac{x - 1}{cos\theta} = \dfrac{y - 2}{sin\theta} = r = \dfrac{6}{3}$

$∴ x = \dfrac{6}{3}cos\theta + 1, y = \dfrac{6}{3}sin\theta + 2$

This point lies on line $x + y = 4$

$∴ \dfrac{6}{3}cos\theta + \dfrac{6}{3}sin\theta = 1$

$⇒ sin\theta + cos\theta = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ sin\left(\dfrac{π}{4} + \theta\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{π}{4} + \theta = 60 °$ or $120 °$

$⇒ \theta = 15 °$~or $75 °$

$∴$ Larger angle $= 75 °$

questions.q: If $(-4,5)$ is one vertex and $7 x-y+8=0$ is one diagonal of a square, then the equation of second diagonal is
questions.solution:
One vertex of square is $(-4,5)$ and equation of one diagonal is $7 x-y+8=0$ Diagonal of a square are perpendicular and bisect each other
Let the equation of the other diagonal be $y=m x+c$ where $m$ is the slope of the line and $c$ is the $\mathrm{y}$-intercept.
Since this line passes through $(-4,5)$


Since this line is at right angle to the line
$7 x-y+8=0$ or $y=7 x+8$, having slope $=7$,
$\therefore 7 \times \mathrm{m}=-1$ or $\mathrm{m}=\frac{-1}{7}$
Putting this value of $m$ in equation (i) we get
$5=-4 \times\left(\frac{-1}{7}\right)+c$
or $5=\frac{4}{7}+c \quad$ or $\quad c=5-\frac{4}{7}=\frac{31}{7}$
Hence equation of the other diagonal is
$y=-\frac{1}{7} x+\frac{31}{7}$ or $7 y=-x+31$ or $x+7 y-31=0$ or $x+7 y=31$

questions.q: If the lines $4 x+3 y-1=0, x-y+5=0$ and $k x+5 y-3=0$ are concurrent, then $k$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Since, the given three lines are concurrent, then
\left|\begin{array}{rrr}4 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 \\ k & 5 & -3\end{array}\right|=0\Rightarrow 4(3-25)-3(-3-5 k)-1(5+k)=0\Rightarrow-88+9+15 k-5-k=0\Rightarrow \quad 14 k=84\therefore \quad k=6

questions.q: The distance of the point \((-1,1)\) from the line \(12(x+6)=5(y-2)\) is
questions.solution:
The given line is \(12(x+6)=5(y-2)\)
\(\Rightarrow 12 x+72=5 y-10\)
or \(12 x-5 y+72+10=0 \Rightarrow 12 x-5 y+82=0\) The perpendicular distance from \(\left($x_1, y_1\right)\) to the line \(a x+b y+c=0\) is \($\frac{\left(\mathrm{ax}_1+\mathrm{by}_1+\mathrm{c}\right)}{\sqrt{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2}}$\). The point \(\left($x_1, y_1\right)\) is \((-1,1)\), therefore, perpendicular distance from \((-1,1)\) to the line \(12 x-5 y+82=0\) is
\(=$\frac{|-12-5+82|}{\sqrt{12^2+(-5)^2}}=\frac{65}{\sqrt{144+25}}=\frac{65}{\sqrt{169}}=$5\)

questions.q: If the distance between the points $(a \cos \theta, a \sin \theta)$ and $(a \cos \phi, a \sin \phi)$ is $2 a$, then $\theta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let the points be $A=(a \cos \theta, a \sin \theta)$ and $\begin{aligned}$& B=(a \cos \phi, a \sin \phi) \\
& \therefore \quad A $B=\sqrt{(a \cos \theta-a \cos \phi)^2}+($a \sin \theta-a \sin \phi)^2 \\
& $=\sqrt{a^2 \cos ^2 \theta+a^2 \cos ^2 \phi-2 a^2 \cos \theta \cos \phi}$\\
& \quad \quad+a^2 \sin ^2 \theta+a^2 \sin ^2 \phi-2 a^2 \sin \theta \sin \phi
\end{aligned} $\begin{aligned}$& $=\sqrt{2 a^2-2 a^2(\cos \theta \cos \phi+\sin \theta \sin \phi)}$\\
& $=\sqrt{2}a(\sqrt{1-\cos (\theta-\phi)}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 $a=\sqrt{2}$a $\sqrt{2} \sin  \left(\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}\right)$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sin \$left(\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}\right)=$1 \Rightarrow $\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}=$n \pi \pm $\frac{\pi}{2}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sin \$left(\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}\right)=$1 \Rightarrow $\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}=$n \pi \pm $\frac{\pi}{2}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad \theta-\phi=2 n \pi \pm \pi \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \theta=2 n \pi \pm \pi+\phi \\
&
\end{aligned} where, $n \in Z$

questions.q: The equation of a given straight line is $\frac{x-x_1}{\cos \theta}=\frac{y-y_1}{\sin \theta}=\gamma$. If the equation of the line perpendicular to the given line and passing through $(\alpha, \beta)$ is $\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=1$, then $\frac{b}{a}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given equation of line is $\frac{x-x_1}{\cos \theta}=\frac{y-y_1}{\sin \theta}=\gamma$ Slope of Eq. (i) is $m=\tan \theta$
So, slope of a line perpendicular to Eq. (i) is $(-\cot \theta)$. According to the question, equation of required line is $\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=1$ Slope of line (ii) is \left(\frac{-b}{a}\right)$ So, $\frac{-b}{a}=-\cot \theta \Rightarrow \frac{b}{a}=\cot \theta$

questions.q: A straight line passing through a fixed point  \left(3, 5\right)$ intersects the coordinate axes at two~points $A$ and $B .$~If the locus of $C  \left(x, y\right)$ which forms a rectangle with the points $A, O$~(origin) and $B$ is $ax + 2hxy + by = 0$~then $a + b + h =
questions.solution:
⇒ \dfrac{3}{p} + \dfrac{5}{q} =1$

Here, coordinate~of point are~$C ( x, y ) = ( p, q )$

Hence, to find locus of~$C$~substitute~$p = x \text{ and } q = y$~in the above equation.

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{5}{y} =1$

$⇒ 5x + 3y - xy = 0$

Now compare~$ax + by + 2hxy = 0$to $5x + 3y - xy = 0$

$a = 5b = 3, h = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$a + b + h ⇒ 5 + 3 - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{15}{2}.$

questions.q: The number of possible straight lines passing through the point $(2,3)$, while forming a triangle with coordinate axes enclosing an area 12 sq. units is
questions.solution: Let the equation of line forming a triangle having area $12 \mathrm{sq}$. units is $\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=$1 So, |a b|=24 $\because$ Line (i) passes through point $(2,3)$, so $\frac{2}{a}+\frac{3}{b}=$1 from Eqs. (ii) and (iii), we get |2 b+3 a|=24 If $a$ and $b$ are positive, then $\begin{array}{rlrl}$& & a b=24 $\text { and }$3 a+2 b=24 \\ \Rightarrow & a\left(\frac{24-3 a}{2}\right)=$24 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } 3 a²-24 a+48=0 \\ \text{ and } \because $\text { Discriminant }=$24^2-4 $\times$3 $\times$48=0 \\ \therefore \text{ and } a=4 $\text { and }$b=6 \end{array} If $a$ is positive and $b$ is negative then $a b=-24$ and $3 a+2 b=24$. \Rightarrow \quad 2\left(\frac{24-3 a}{2}\right)=-$24 \Rightarrow 3 a²-24 a-48=0 $\because$ Discriminant $=24^2+4 \times 3 \times 48>0\begin{array}{ll} \therefore \quad$a=$\frac{24 \pm \sqrt{2 \times 24^2}}{6}=$4+4 $\sqrt{2} \quad \because$a>0 \\ $\text { and } \quad$b=6-6 $\sqrt{2} \end{array}$If $a$ is negative and $b$ is positive, then $a b=-24$ and $3 a+2 b=24$ \Rightarrow \quad a=4-4 $\sqrt{2} \text { and }$b=6+6 $\sqrt{2}$And at the last it is not possible that $a$ and $b$ both are negative. So, 3 triangles are possible.

questions.q: $P$ is a point inside the $\Delta ABC$. Three straight lines parallel to $AB, BC$ and $AC$ are drawn which divides the triangle into six regions. If the area of three triangles formed in these regions are $9,16$ and $25$ square units, then the area (in sq. units) of $\Delta ABC$ is
questions.solution:
$∵ \Delta ABC, \Delta TUP, \Delta PDE, \Delta SPR$ all are similar
$∴ratioofareas = \left(ratioofsides\right)2$
Let, $PT = \alpha = AS$
$∴\dfrac{SR}{PT} = \dfrac{4}{5} ⇒ SR = \dfrac{4\alpha}{5}$
$\dfrac{PE}{PT} = \dfrac{3}{5} ⇒ PE = \dfrac{3\alpha}{5}$
$⇒ AC = AS + SR + RC$
$= \alpha + \dfrac{4\alpha}{5} + \dfrac{3\alpha}{5}$
$= \dfrac{12\alpha}{5}$
$∴ \dfrac{ar\left(\Delta ABC\right)}{ar\left(\Delta PDE\right)} = \dfrac{{\left(AC\right)}^{2}}{{\left(PE\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{1{2}^{2} \cdot {\alpha}^{2}}{{5}^{2} \cdot \left(\dfrac{{3}^{2}{\alpha}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}\right)}$
Hence, $ar\left(\Delta ABC\right) = 16ar\left(\Delta PDE\right) = 144sq . units$

questions.solution:
Let, the centroid be& \left(x, y\right),$~then

$x = \dfrac{acosk + bsink + 1}{3}$~&~$y = \dfrac{asink - bcosk + 0}{3}$

$⇒ 3x - 1 = acosk + bsink . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ 3y = asink - bcosk . . . \left(ii\right)$

Square~ \left($i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$~then add~ we get,

$⇒\left(3x - 1\right)2 + \left(3y\right)2 = a^{2} + b^{2}$

$

questions.q: The equation of the line passing through the point of intersection of the lines $x-3 y+2=0$ and $2 x+5 y-7=0$ and perpendicular to the line $3 x+2 y+5=0$ is :
questions.solution:
The equation of lines are $x-3 y+2=0$ ...(i)
and $2 x+5 y-7=0$ ...(ii)
On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$x=1, y=1\therefore$ The co-ordinates of a point of intersection of given lines are $(1,1)$.
The equation of line perpendicular to $3 x+2 y+5=0$ is $2 x-3 y+\lambda=0$.
Which passes through $(1,1)$.
$\therefore \quad 2-3+\lambda=0\Rightarrow \quad \lambda=1\therefore$ Required equation of line is
$2 x-3 y+1=0$

questions.q: If the sides of a triangle are given by the equations& $x - y + 1 = 0, x + y + 3 = 0$ and $2x + 5y - 2 = 0$, then the coordinates of its orthocentre are
questions.solution:
As two lines are perpendicular, so triangle is right angle $\Delta$~where right angle is made at point of intersection of these two lines.
Also in right angle triangle, orthocentre is point of intersection of perpendicular lines.
$⇒$ orthocentre is point of intersection of lines~$x - y + 1 = 0$ and $x + y + 3 = 0$~i.e. \left(- 2, - 1\right)$

questions.solution:
There are two points $A$ & $B$ which are at a distance of $10$ units from $P$ and farthest ( $10$ unit distance) from the line $4x + 3y = 17 .$

The slope of $AB = \dfrac{3}{4}$ {Because the slope of $4x + 3y = 17$ is $- \dfrac{4}{3}$ }
Let line $AB$ makes an angle $\theta$ with $x$-axis then $tan ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{3}{4} ⇒ \left(cos ⁡ \theta,sin ⁡ \theta\right) = $\$left(\dfrac{4}{5}, \dfrac{3}{5}\right)$
$⇒ A$ or $B = \left($10cos ⁡ $\theta -$1,10sin ⁡ $\theta +$7\right)$ or $⇒ A$ or $B = \left(-$10cos ⁡ $\theta -$1, - 10sin ⁡ $\theta +$7\right)$
$⇒ A$ or $B = \left(7,13\right)$ or \left(- 9,1\right)

$

questions.q: If the centroid and circumcenter of a triangle are&  \left(3, 3\right)$,~  \left(6, 2\right)$, respectively,& then the orthocentre of the triangle is _____.
questions.solution:
The orthocenter, centroid and circumcenter& of the triangle are collinear and lie on the line called Euler Line.

Also the centroid divides the line joining orthocenter and circumcenter& in the ratio $2: 1 .$

So centroid \left(3, 3\right)$~would be dividing \left(x, y\right)$ and \left(6, 2\right)$ in the ratio of $2: 1 .$

So,~\left(12 + x\right)3 = 3$, therefore $x = 9 - 12 = - 3,$~and \left(4 + y\right)3 = 3,$~therefore $y = 5$.

Hence,~\left(- 3, 5\right)$ is the answer.

questions.q: The area of a triangle is $5.$ If two of its vertices are  \left(2, 1\right), \left(3, - 2\right)$ and the third vertex lies on the line $y = x + 3$, then the third vertex is -$
questions.solution:
Let the third vertex be \left(h, k\right)$

Since it lies on line $y = x + 3$

$∴ k = h + 3$ ........(1)

Also area of triangle is $5$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{2}\left[2\left(- 2 - k\right) + 3\left(k - 1\right) + h\left(1 + 2\right)\right] = \pm 5$

$⇒ k + 3h - 7 = \pm 10$ ........(2)

Solving (1) & (2) we get

$h = \dfrac{7}{2}, k = \dfrac{13}{2} ⇒ \left(\dfrac{7}{2}, \dfrac{13}{2}\right)

and $h = $\dfrac{- 3}{2},$k = $\dfrac{3}{2}$⇒ \left(- \dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$

questions.solution:
Let& $A ≡ \left(-2, 0\right), B = \left(-1, \dfrac{1}{3}\right),C ≡ $\$lleft(cos\theta,sin\theta\right)

Equation to~$AB,$

$y - 0 = \left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3} - 0}{- 1 + 2}\right)\left($x + 2\right)$

$⇒ $\sqrt{3}$y = x + 2,$~Point C lies on this line.

$⇒ $\sqrt{3}$sin\theta -cos\theta =2$

\theta - $\dfrac{π}{6} = \dfrac{π}{2}$
